Energy transition

The End of an Era

Two coal plants power your Pittsburgh utility. They're getting older, and a replacement can take years to build. Your customers can switch suppliers sooner than that.

Play The End of an Era↗ Your decisions ↓

Choose your difficulty before you start. It’s free to play in your browser.

Location
Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania
Starts in
1980
Your term
20 years

Your starting point

In 1980 you inherit coal plants of different ages. The older equipment will lose output, and new rules will eventually make coal more expensive to run.

Those plants also earn the revenue you need to replace them. You have twenty years to decide how long to run each one and what to build in its place.

Learn how to play

Your decisions

  1. 01

    Choose which plant to replace first

    Look at each unit's age and output. Start the replacement early enough to supply customers when the old plant slows down.

  2. 02

    Compare what the new plants can supply

    Check both the construction price and the hours each project can cover. A cheap source of daytime power still leaves the night to plan for.

  3. 03

    Keep customers through the change

    Check the rates and reliability you're offering. Each customer who leaves takes some of your construction budget with them.
